# OPERATIONAL_PLAYBOOKS.md

Last Updated: 2026-06-29

# PURPOSE

This document defines the canonical Operational Playbooks for the Global Authority for AI Governance (GAFAIG).

It establishes the deterministic operational procedures governing how authorized participants perform operational work throughout the complete applicant lifecycle.

Operational Playbooks translate the canonical operational architecture into standardized operational execution.

Operational Playbooks define operational procedures only.

Operational Playbooks do not establish constitutional authority.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# STATUS

This is a canonical architecture document for the Operational Experience Architecture era.

It defines operational procedures only.

It complements workflow architecture, participant architecture, navigation architecture, decision architecture, responsibility architecture, workflow state management, and Case Workspace architecture.

---

# RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER DOCUMENTS

This document is subordinate to the constitutional governance architecture.

It complements:

* OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOW_ARCHITECTURE.md
* OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOW_STATE_MACHINE.md
* OPERATIONAL_PARTICIPANT_ARCHITECTURE.md
* OPERATIONAL_NAVIGATION_ARCHITECTURE.md

* CASE_WORKSPACE_ARCHITECTURE.md

The Operational Playbooks define standardized operational execution based upon these canonical architectural documents.

# DESIGN OBJECTIVES

Operational Playbooks shall ensure:

* Deterministic operational execution.
* Consistent participant behavior.
* Standardized operational procedures.
* Repeatable workflow execution.
* Clear operational guidance.
* Explicit responsibility.
* Constitutional authority preservation.
* Complete operational auditability.

Every operational procedure shall be:

* Deterministic.
* Repeatable.
* Auditable.
* Role-specific.
* Workflow-driven.
* Constitutionally compliant.

---

# OPERATIONAL PHILOSOPHY

Operational work follows workflow.

Operational work follows constitutional authority.

Operational work follows responsibility.

Operational work follows deterministic guidance.

Operational procedures never depend upon individual preference.

Operational procedures shall produce consistent operational outcomes regardless of participant.

# PASS 2A.1 — APPLICANT OPERATIONAL FOUNDATION

---

# APPLICANT OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK

This playbook defines the canonical operational procedures for Applicants participating in the GAFAIG operational workflow.

The Applicant is responsible for preparing, submitting, maintaining, and responding to all operational activities required for successful certification.

Applicants never perform governance activities.

Applicants never perform certification activities.

Applicants never perform publication activities.

Applicants operate exclusively within constitutionally authorized workflow responsibilities.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# OPERATIONAL PURPOSE

The Applicant prepares and maintains a complete, accurate, and supportable certification case.

The Applicant provides the operational inputs required for deterministic review throughout the applicant lifecycle.

The Applicant's objective is not simply to submit information.

The Applicant's objective is to enable efficient, accurate, and complete operational review through high-quality submissions.

---

# PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

The Applicant shall:

* Prepare an accurate application.
* Maintain organizational information.
* Upload complete supporting evidence.
* Upload supporting artifacts.
* Respond promptly to information requests.
* Resolve deficiencies.
* Submit remediation packages.
* Monitor certification progress.
* Support governance review when requested.
* Maintain repository quality.

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Applicant operations are considered successful when:

* Application information is complete.
* Required repositories are complete.
* Evidence is accurate.
* Artifacts support submitted evidence.
* Information requests are answered completely.
* Deficiencies are resolved promptly.
* Remediation packages satisfy operational requirements.
* Workflow progresses without avoidable delays.
* Certification proceeds without unnecessary operational interruption.

---

# ENTRY CONDITIONS

Applicant operational work begins when:

* Organization account is established.
* Applicant authentication succeeds.
* Organization authorization is verified.
* Applicant Dashboard becomes available.

The Applicant begins all operational work from the Dashboard.

---

# DAILY OPERATIONAL WORKFLOW

The Applicant should perform the following operational sequence each working session.

1. Sign in.
2. Review Dashboard.
3. Review Notifications.
4. Review assigned Cases.
5. Open active Case Workspace.
6. Review Current Stage.
7. Review Next Required Action.
8. Review Waiting Conditions.
9. Complete required repository activities.
10. Verify operational completeness.
11. Exit the workflow only after required work is complete.

Applicants should avoid navigating directly to repositories without first reviewing the Case Workspace.

---

# CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Applicant is currently responsible for:

* Application preparation.
* Evidence submission.
* Artifact submission.
* Repository completeness.
* Information request responses.
* Deficiency responses.
* Remediation preparation.
* Operational communication.
* Certification monitoring.

Applicants remain responsible until workflow ownership transfers through deterministic workflow progression.

---

# SUPPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES

Applicants also support:

* Operational Review.
* Governance Review.
* Certification preparation.

Support may include:

* Clarifications.
* Repository updates.
* Additional documentation.
* Corrected submissions.
* Organizational coordination.

Support does not transfer workflow ownership.

---

# REPOSITORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Applicants maintain responsibility for:

Evidence Repository

* Upload evidence.
* Organize evidence.
* Replace incorrect evidence.
* Verify evidence completeness.

Artifact Repository

* Upload supporting artifacts.
* Maintain artifact organization.
* Verify artifact quality.

Information Request Repository

* Review requests.
* Submit complete responses.

Remediation Repository

* Prepare remediation.
* Upload remediation documentation.
* Submit remediation.

Progress Repository

* Monitor workflow progression.
* Monitor repository completion.

---

# DECISION RESPONSIBILITIES

Applicants do not create constitutional decisions.

Applicants support decisions by:

* Providing evidence.
* Providing documentation.
* Responding to requests.
* Resolving deficiencies.
* Submitting remediation.

Applicants prepare decision inputs only.

Decision authority remains with authorized GAFAIG participants.

---

# COMMUNICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

Applicants shall communicate through authorized operational channels.

Communication includes:

* Information request responses.
* Repository submissions.
* Remediation submissions.
* Organizational updates.

Applicants shall avoid unofficial communication channels for operational matters.

---

# NOTIFICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

Applicants shall review notifications at the beginning of every operational session.

Notifications may include:

* New information requests.
* Deficiency notices.
* Remediation requests.
* Repository updates.
* Workflow progression.
* Certification status.
* Operational reminders.

Unread operational notifications should be reviewed before beginning new repository work.

---

# WAITING CONDITIONS

Applicants may encounter waiting conditions including:

* Operational Review in progress.
* Governance Review in progress.
* Certification processing.
* Publication processing.
* Information request evaluation.
* Remediation review.

During waiting conditions the Applicant should:

* Monitor notifications.
* Review workflow progress.
* Prepare requested materials.
* Avoid duplicate submissions unless instructed.

---

# ESCALATION PROCEDURES

Applicants should escalate operational issues only when:

* Required operational functionality is unavailable.
* Authorized repository access fails.
* Workflow appears blocked without explanation.
* Information requests cannot be completed.
* Repository uploads repeatedly fail.
* Organizational authorization issues prevent required work.

Escalation should follow established GAFAIG operational procedures.

---

# OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Applicants should:

* Maintain repository quality.
* Respond promptly.
* Minimize operational delays.
* Avoid duplicate submissions.
* Maintain organized documentation.
* Review operational guidance before taking action.

Well-prepared applicants contribute directly to efficient operational review.

---

# OPERATIONAL FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

Applicants shall always remember:

* Workflow determines operational activity.
* The Case Workspace is the primary operational workspace.
* Repositories support workflow.
* Decisions belong to authorized reviewers.
* Responsibility transfers only through deterministic workflow progression.
* Notifications communicate operational changes.
* Navigation supports workflow rather than replacing it.

---

# AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES

Applicants shall never:

* Perform governance review.
* Record governance findings.
* Issue deficiencies.
* Accept remediation.
* Issue certifications.
* Authorize publication.
* Modify constitutional records.
* Override Snowflake-backed operational data.

Applicants participate exclusively within constitutionally authorized operational responsibilities.

---

# TRANSITION TO SCREEN-BY-SCREEN GUIDANCE

The following section defines deterministic operational guidance for every Applicant workspace.

Each operational screen specifies:

* Purpose.
* Entry conditions.
* Review priorities.
* Required operational activities.
* Success indicators.
* Warning indicators.
* Exit conditions.
* Next navigation.

These procedures establish standardized operational behavior throughout the complete Applicant operational experience.

END PASS 2A.1

# PASS 2A.2 — APPLICANT SCREEN-BY-SCREEN OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE

---

# APPLICANT DASHBOARD

## Purpose

The Applicant Dashboard provides operational awareness for all current applicant activities.

It is the required starting point for every operational session.

---

## When to Open

Open the Dashboard:

* Immediately after signing in.
* At the beginning of every work session.
* After completing major operational activities.
* After receiving notifications.
* After workflow stage transitions.

---

## Review First

Always review, in order:

1. Notifications.
2. Active Cases.
3. Current Workflow Stage.
4. Next Required Action.
5. Waiting Conditions.
6. Repository Status.
7. Certification Status.

---

## Success Indicators

The Dashboard indicates healthy workflow when:

* No overdue activities exist.
* No unresolved notifications exist.
* Active cases display current workflow status.
* Required actions are clearly identified.
* Repository summaries indicate expected progress.

---

## Warning Indicators

Review immediately if:

* New Information Request appears.
* Deficiency Notice exists.
* Repository marked incomplete.
* Workflow appears stalled.
* Certification status changes unexpectedly.
* Notifications remain unread.

---

## Required Actions

Applicants should:

* Review notifications.
* Select highest-priority active case.
* Open the Case Workspace.
* Complete the displayed Next Required Action.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Ignoring notifications.
* Beginning new submissions before reviewing current workflow.
* Navigating directly to repositories.
* Uploading duplicate information.

---

## Next Navigation

Dashboard

↓

My Cases

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Dashboard review is complete when:

* Notifications reviewed.
* Active case selected.
* Case Workspace opened.

---

# MY CASES

## Purpose

Provide access to every applicant case associated with the organization.

---

## When to Open

Open when:

* Selecting work.
* Reviewing case history.
* Monitoring multiple cases.
* Returning to previously active work.

---

## Review First

Review:

* Current Stage.
* Current Status.
* Current Owner.
* Last Activity.
* Next Required Action.

---

## Success Indicators

Cases display:

* Accurate workflow stage.
* Expected status.
* Current ownership.
* Current timestamps.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Case remains unchanged for extended periods.
* Waiting state appears unexpectedly.
* Status conflicts with recent submissions.
* Required action is unclear.

---

## Required Actions

Select the active case requiring attention.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Opening completed cases unnecessarily.
* Working on inactive cases.
* Ignoring workflow priority.

---

## Next Navigation

My Cases

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Correct Case Workspace opened.

---

# CASE WORKSPACE

## Purpose

The Case Workspace is the primary operational workspace.

All operational work begins and ends here.

---

## When to Open

Always before interacting with repositories.

---

## Review First

Review in this order:

1. Current Workflow Stage.
2. Current Responsible Participant.
3. Next Required Action.
4. Waiting Conditions.
5. Repository Summary.
6. Timeline.
7. Notifications.

---

## Success Indicators

Case Workspace displays:

* Current workflow stage.
* Clear next action.
* Repository health.
* No unexplained workflow issues.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Repository incomplete.
* Waiting condition exists.
* Required repository unavailable.
* Unexpected workflow stage displayed.

---

## Required Actions

Perform only the Next Required Action.

Avoid performing work outside the current workflow stage.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Uploading unnecessary repositories.
* Attempting future workflow activities.
* Ignoring repository summaries.

---

## Next Navigation

Repository required by workflow.

---

## Exit Criteria

Required operational activity completed.

---

# EVIDENCE REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Maintain evidence supporting operational review.

---

## When to Open

Only when evidence activities are required.

---

## Review First

Review:

* Missing evidence.
* Existing evidence.
* Evidence organization.
* Submission completeness.

---

## Success Indicators

Evidence repository contains:

* Required evidence.
* Correct evidence.
* Organized documentation.
* No duplicate submissions.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Evidence missing.
* Incorrect document uploaded.
* Duplicate evidence exists.
* Validation issues reported.

---

## Required Actions

Upload, replace, or organize evidence as required.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Uploading duplicate files.
* Uploading incorrect document versions.
* Leaving required evidence incomplete.

---

## Next Navigation

Return to Case Workspace.

---

## Exit Criteria

Evidence repository complete.

---

# ARTIFACT REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Maintain supporting operational artifacts.

## Review First

* Required artifacts.
* Existing artifacts.
* Artifact completeness.

## Required Actions

Upload required supporting artifacts.

## Exit Criteria

Artifact repository complete.

---

# INFORMATION REQUESTS

## Purpose

Respond to formal operational requests.

## Review First

* Open requests.
* Requested information.
* Response deadlines.

## Required Actions

Prepare complete response.

Submit requested information.

## Exit Criteria

Request submitted.

---

# DEFICIENCIES

## Purpose

Resolve identified operational deficiencies.

## Review First

* Deficiency description.
* Required corrective action.
* Supporting repositories.

## Required Actions

Prepare complete remediation.

## Exit Criteria

Deficiency addressed.

---

# REMEDIATION WORKSPACE

## Purpose

Prepare remediation submissions.

## Review First

* Outstanding deficiencies.
* Required documentation.
* Supporting repositories.

## Required Actions

Submit remediation.

## Exit Criteria

Remediation submitted.

---

# CERTIFICATION STATUS

## Purpose

Monitor certification lifecycle.

## Review First

* Certification status.
* Current workflow stage.
* Pending activities.

Applicants monitor only.

Applicants never modify certification records.

---

# PROGRESS REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Monitor workflow progression.

## Review First

* Current stage.
* Completed stages.
* Waiting stages.
* Timeline.

## Required Actions

Review progress.

Return to Case Workspace.

# PASS 2A.3 — APPLICANT OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

---

# APPLICANT OPERATIONAL CHECKLIST

The following checklist shall be completed during every operational work session.

### Session Startup

□ Authenticate successfully.

□ Open Applicant Dashboard.

□ Review all unread notifications.

□ Review active cases.

□ Review Current Workflow Stage.

□ Review Next Required Action.

□ Review Waiting Conditions.

---

### Case Preparation

□ Open the active Case Workspace.

□ Verify organizational information.

□ Confirm repository summaries.

□ Review outstanding requests.

□ Review outstanding deficiencies.

□ Review current certification status.

---

### Repository Activities

Before uploading any information:

□ Verify the correct case is open.

□ Verify the correct repository is selected.

□ Verify the document is the latest approved version.

□ Verify duplicate submissions are not being created.

□ Verify uploaded information belongs to the current organization.

After uploading:

□ Confirm upload completed successfully.

□ Confirm repository status updated.

□ Confirm uploaded document appears correctly.

---

### Information Request Responses

Before responding:

□ Read the complete request.

□ Identify every requested item.

□ Verify supporting documentation.

□ Prepare complete responses.

Before submission:

□ Verify all requested information has been addressed.

□ Confirm supporting evidence has been attached.

□ Review for accuracy.

---

### Deficiency Resolution

Before beginning remediation:

□ Read every deficiency completely.

□ Identify root cause.

□ Prepare corrective documentation.

□ Verify remediation addresses every identified issue.

Before submission:

□ Confirm deficiency response is complete.

□ Confirm remediation documentation is attached.

□ Confirm repository updates are complete.

---

### Workflow Completion

Before ending a work session:

□ Review Case Workspace.

□ Confirm no additional required actions remain.

□ Confirm notifications reviewed.

□ Confirm repository status is current.

□ Confirm workflow stage reflects completed work.

---

# APPLICANT VALIDATION CHECKLIST

Applicants shall validate:

Organization

□ Organization information accurate.

Application

□ Application complete.

Evidence

□ Required evidence uploaded.

Artifacts

□ Required artifacts uploaded.

Repositories

□ Repository summaries accurate.

Requests

□ Information requests answered completely.

Deficiencies

□ All deficiencies addressed.

Remediation

□ Remediation documentation complete.

Progress

□ Workflow progression verified.

---

# QUALITY ASSURANCE CHECKLIST

Before submitting operational work, Applicants should confirm:

Accuracy

□ Information is correct.

Completeness

□ Nothing required is missing.

Consistency

□ Submitted information is internally consistent.

Readability

□ Documentation is understandable.

Traceability

□ Supporting evidence clearly supports submitted information.

Organization

□ Repository organization is logical.

---

# COMPLETION CRITERIA

Applicant operational work is complete when:

* Required activities completed.
* Required repositories complete.
* Information requests satisfied.
* Deficiencies addressed.
* Remediation submitted when required.
* Current workflow stage reflects expected progression.
* Next Required Action belongs to another participant.

Completion does not imply certification.

Completion indicates Applicant responsibilities for the current workflow stage have concluded.

---

# RESPONSIBILITY HANDOFF

When Applicant responsibilities conclude:

Responsibility transfers through deterministic workflow progression.

Typical handoffs include:

Applicant

↓

GAFAIG Intake Reviewer

or

Applicant

↓

GAFAIG Operations Reviewer

depending upon workflow stage.

Applicants shall verify:

* Required repositories complete.
* Notifications reviewed.
* Outstanding tasks resolved.

Applicants shall not manually transfer workflow ownership.

---

# OPERATIONAL BEST PRACTICES

Applicants should:

* Work from the Case Workspace.
* Review notifications before beginning work.
* Submit complete documentation.
* Organize repositories logically.
* Respond promptly to requests.
* Avoid duplicate uploads.
* Maintain document version control.
* Review all submissions before finalizing.

Consistent operational discipline reduces review delays.

---

# COMMON OPERATIONAL ERRORS

Applicants should avoid:

* Uploading duplicate evidence.

* Uploading incorrect document versions.

* Ignoring notifications.

* Responding to only part of an information request.

* Beginning remediation before understanding deficiencies.

* Uploading documentation into the wrong repository.

* Assuming workflow has progressed without verification.

* Attempting to bypass workflow stages.

---

# OPERATIONAL RECOVERY PROCEDURES

When problems occur:

Repository upload failure

→ Verify network connectivity.

→ Retry upload.

→ Confirm repository status.

Missing documentation

→ Review repository summary.

→ Upload missing documentation.

Workflow appears stalled

→ Review Waiting Conditions.

→ Review notifications.

→ Determine Current Responsible Participant.

Unexpected workflow state

→ Review timeline.

→ Verify recent submissions.

→ Contact GAFAIG operations if necessary.

---

# APPLICANT PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Applicants are expected to:

* Maintain complete repositories.
* Respond within required operational timeframes.
* Preserve documentation quality.
* Maintain accurate organizational information.
* Cooperate throughout operational review.
* Support efficient workflow progression.

---

# FUTURE AUTOMATION ASSISTANCE

Future automation may assist Applicants by:

* Identifying missing evidence.

* Detecting incomplete repositories.

* Highlighting outstanding requests.

* Identifying unresolved deficiencies.

* Monitoring workflow progress.

* Recommending Next Required Actions.

Automation shall never:

* Submit repositories automatically.

* Create governance findings.

* Approve certification.

* Publish registry records.

* Override Applicant decisions.

Automation remains advisory only.

---

# APPLICANT OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK COMPLETION

The Applicant Operational Playbook is complete when the Applicant can consistently determine:

* What work requires attention.

* Which screen should be used.

* Which repository requires action.

* What documentation must be prepared.

* What constitutes successful completion.

* When responsibility transfers.

* What happens next.

This playbook establishes the canonical operational procedures for every Applicant participating in the GAFAIG Operational Workflow.

END PASS 2A.3

# PASS 2B.1 — ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR OPERATIONAL FOUNDATION

---

# ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK

This playbook defines the canonical operational procedures for Organization Administrators participating in the GAFAIG operational workflow.

The Organization Administrator coordinates organizational participation throughout the complete applicant lifecycle.

The Organization Administrator manages organizational readiness, participant coordination, repository oversight, and operational communication.

The Organization Administrator does not perform governance activities.

The Organization Administrator does not perform certification activities.

The Organization Administrator does not perform publication activities.

The Organization Administrator operates exclusively within constitutionally authorized workflow responsibilities.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# OPERATIONAL PURPOSE

The Organization Administrator coordinates all operational activities performed by the organization.

The Organization Administrator ensures the organization remains prepared, responsive, organized, and operationally aligned throughout certification.

The Organization Administrator serves as the operational coordinator rather than the constitutional decision maker.

---

# PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

The Organization Administrator shall:

* Coordinate applicant activities.
* Coordinate Evidence Contributors.
* Monitor organizational operational readiness.
* Verify repository completeness.
* Ensure timely responses to operational requests.
* Coordinate remediation activities.
* Monitor workflow progression.
* Maintain organizational communication.
* Support successful certification preparation.
* Reduce operational delays.

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Organization Administrator operations are considered successful when:

* Organizational participants remain coordinated.
* Repository activities remain organized.
* Required submissions occur on schedule.
* Information requests are answered promptly.
* Deficiencies are addressed efficiently.
* Repository quality remains high.
* Workflow progresses without organizational delays.
* Communication remains consistent.
* Certification progresses without unnecessary interruption.

---

# ENTRY CONDITIONS

Organization Administrator operational work begins when:

* Organization authentication succeeds.
* Organization authorization is verified.
* Administrative privileges are confirmed.
* Organization Dashboard becomes available.

Every operational session begins from the Dashboard.

---

# DAILY OPERATIONAL WORKFLOW

The Organization Administrator should perform the following operational sequence during every working session.

1. Sign in.
2. Review Dashboard.
3. Review Notifications.
4. Review Organizational Cases.
5. Review Current Workflow Stages.
6. Review Outstanding Requests.
7. Review Outstanding Deficiencies.
8. Review Repository Health.
9. Coordinate required organizational activities.
10. Verify operational completeness.
11. Review responsibility handoffs.

---

# CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Organization Administrator is currently responsible for:

* Organizational coordination.
* Participant coordination.
* Repository oversight.
* Submission monitoring.
* Communication coordination.
* Workflow monitoring.
* Operational readiness.
* Internal organization support.
* Certification preparation support.

The Organization Administrator coordinates operational work but does not replace participant ownership.

---

# SUPPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES

The Organization Administrator supports:

* Applicant.
* Evidence Contributors.
* GAFAIG Intake Reviewer.
* GAFAIG Operations Reviewer.

Support activities include:

* Organizational coordination.
* Repository preparation.
* Documentation collection.
* Internal communication.
* Submission readiness.
* Scheduling operational work.

Supporting responsibilities never transfer workflow ownership.

Artifact Repository

Information Request Repository

* Monitor organizational readiness.

* Repository readiness.
* Submission quality.
* Communication.
* Operational planning.

Decision authority remains with authorized GAFAIG operational participants.

# COMMUNICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Organization Administrator coordinates official organizational communication.

Communication responsibilities include:

* Coordinating repository preparation.
* Coordinating information request responses.
* Coordinating remediation.
* Communicating workflow expectations.
* Coordinating internal operational activities.

Operational communication shall remain accurate, timely, and organization-wide.

# NOTIFICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Organization Administrator shall review notifications at the beginning of every operational session.

Notifications may include:

* New applicant activity.
* Repository updates.
* Information requests.
* Deficiency notices.
* Workflow progression.
* Operational reminders.
* Certification updates.
* Organizational alerts.

Unread notifications should always be reviewed before assigning organizational work.

# WAITING CONDITIONS

Organization Administrators may encounter waiting conditions including:

* Applicant preparation.
* Evidence collection.
* Repository updates.
* Operational review.
* Governance review.
* Certification processing.
* Publication processing.

During waiting conditions the Organization Administrator should:

* Coordinate internal readiness.
* Monitor workflow progression.
* Prepare upcoming activities.
* Review organizational repository status.
* Avoid duplicate submissions.

---

# ESCALATION PROCEDURES

The Organization Administrator should escalate operational issues when:

* Organizational participation becomes blocked.
* Repository completion cannot proceed.
* Required organizational information is unavailable.
* Operational workflow appears stalled.
* Multiple repository failures occur.
* Organization authorization issues prevent progress.

Escalation shall follow established GAFAIG operational procedures.

---

# OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Organization Administrators are expected to:

* Maintain organizational readiness.
* Coordinate participant activities.
* Promote repository quality.
* Minimize operational delays.
* Ensure timely communication.
* Support efficient workflow progression.
* Maintain operational discipline.

Effective organizational coordination contributes directly to efficient operational review.

---

# OPERATIONAL FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

Organization Administrators shall always remember:

* Workflow determines operational activity.
* Coordination supports workflow.
* The Case Workspace remains the operational center.
* Repository readiness supports operational review.
* Decisions belong to authorized reviewers.
* Responsibility transfers only through deterministic workflow progression.
* Organizational coordination improves operational efficiency.

# AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES

Organization Administrators shall never:

* Perform governance review.
* Record governance findings.
* Accept or reject evidence.
* Issue deficiencies.
* Approve remediation.
* Issue certifications.
* Publish registry records.
* Modify constitutional records.
* Override Snowflake-backed operational data.

Organization Administrators participate exclusively within constitutionally authorized operational responsibilities.

# PASS 2B.3 — ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES

---

# ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR OPERATIONAL CHECKLIST

The following checklist shall be completed during every operational work session.

### Session Startup

□ Authenticate successfully.

□ Open Organization Administrator Dashboard.

□ Review all unread notifications.

□ Review organizational cases.

□ Review Current Workflow Stages.

□ Review organizational priorities.

□ Review Waiting Conditions.

---

### Organizational Coordination

□ Review active Applicants.

□ Review Evidence Contributor activities.

□ Review repository summaries.

□ Review outstanding Information Requests.

□ Review outstanding Deficiencies.

□ Review pending Remediation.

□ Verify internal organizational assignments.

---

### Repository Oversight

Before coordinating repository work:

□ Verify the correct case is open.

□ Verify repository summaries are current.

□ Verify required submissions remain outstanding.

□ Verify no duplicate submissions are being prepared.

□ Verify repository ownership is understood.

After repository updates:

□ Confirm repository status reflects new activity.

□ Confirm organizational participants have completed assigned work.

□ Confirm repository readiness.

---

### Information Request Coordination

Before coordinating responses:

□ Review the complete Information Request.

□ Identify responsible organizational participants.

□ Assign response preparation.

□ Verify supporting documentation.

Before submission:

□ Confirm all requested information has been addressed.

□ Confirm evidence supports every response.

□ Verify organizational completeness.

---

### Deficiency Coordination

Before beginning remediation coordination:

□ Review every identified deficiency.

□ Identify required organizational participants.

□ Assign corrective activities.

□ Verify remediation plan.

Before submission:

□ Confirm all deficiencies addressed.

□ Confirm supporting documentation attached.

□ Confirm repository updates complete.

---

### Workflow Completion

Before ending a work session:

□ Review Case Workspace.

□ Verify organizational work is current.

□ Confirm notifications reviewed.

□ Confirm repository status updated.

□ Confirm workflow progression reflects completed coordination.

---

# ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR VALIDATION CHECKLIST

Organization Administrators shall validate:

Organization

□ Organizational information current.

Participants

□ Required participants assigned.

Repositories

□ Repository summaries accurate.

Evidence

□ Evidence preparation coordinated.

Artifacts

□ Artifact preparation coordinated.

Information Requests

□ Responses coordinated.

Deficiencies

□ Corrective activities assigned.

Remediation

□ Remediation preparation complete.

Progress

□ Workflow progression verified.

---

# QUALITY ASSURANCE CHECKLIST

Before organizational work is considered complete:

Accuracy

□ Organizational information correct.

Completeness

□ Required organizational activities completed.

Consistency

□ Organizational participants aligned.

Communication

□ Internal communication complete.

Repository Quality

□ Repository readiness verified.

Coordination

□ Organizational work properly synchronized.

---

# COMPLETION CRITERIA

Organization Administrator operational work is complete when:

* Organizational participants coordinated.
* Repository readiness verified.
* Required submissions coordinated.
* Internal communication completed.
* Workflow progression verified.
* Outstanding organizational tasks resolved.
* Next Required Action belongs to another participant.

Completion does not imply Applicant completion.

Completion indicates organizational coordination responsibilities for the current workflow stage have concluded.

---

# RESPONSIBILITY HANDOFF

Organization Administrator responsibilities conclude through deterministic workflow progression.

Typical handoffs include:

Organization Administrator

↓

Applicant

or

Organization Administrator

↓

Evidence Contributor

or

Organization Administrator

↓

GAFAIG Operations Reviewer

depending upon workflow stage.

Organization Administrators shall verify:

* Organizational coordination complete.
* Repository readiness confirmed.
* Internal assignments complete.
* Outstanding coordination issues resolved.

Organization Administrators shall never manually transfer workflow ownership.

---

# OPERATIONAL BEST PRACTICES

Organization Administrators should:

* Coordinate before directing work.
* Monitor workflow continuously.
* Maintain clear organizational communication.
* Verify repository readiness regularly.
* Resolve issues early.
* Keep documentation organized.
* Review notifications frequently.
* Support efficient operational progression.

Effective coordination reduces operational delays.

---

# COMMON OPERATIONAL ERRORS

Organization Administrators should avoid:

* Delaying internal communication.

* Assigning duplicate work.

* Ignoring repository readiness.

* Overlooking waiting conditions.

* Coordinating activities outside the current workflow stage.

* Assuming work is complete without verification.

* Attempting reviewer responsibilities.

---

# OPERATIONAL RECOVERY PROCEDURES

When problems occur:

Repository not progressing

→ Review repository summaries.

→ Determine responsible participant.

→ Coordinate corrective activities.

Applicant inactive

→ Review notifications.

→ Verify organizational communication.

→ Determine blocking conditions.

Information Request delayed

→ Review organizational assignments.

→ Verify supporting documentation.

Workflow appears stalled

→ Review Case Workspace.

→ Review Waiting Conditions.

→ Determine Current Responsible Participant.

---

# ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Organization Administrators are expected to:

* Maintain organizational readiness.

* Coordinate participants effectively.

* Promote repository quality.

* Minimize operational delays.

* Support efficient workflow progression.

* Preserve organizational accountability.

---

# FUTURE AUTOMATION ASSISTANCE

Future automation may assist Organization Administrators by:

* Monitoring organizational readiness.

* Identifying blocked participants.

* Detecting incomplete repositories.

* Highlighting overdue coordination.

* Monitoring workflow progression.

* Recommending coordination priorities.

Automation shall never:

* Assign constitutional authority.

* Replace organizational decision making.

* Override participant responsibilities.

Automation remains advisory only.

# ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATOR OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK COMPLETION

# PASS 2C.1 — EVIDENCE CONTRIBUTOR OPERATIONAL FOUNDATION

---

# EVIDENCE CONTRIBUTOR OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK

This playbook defines the canonical operational procedures for Evidence Contributors participating in the GAFAIG operational workflow.

The Evidence Contributor prepares, organizes, validates, and submits evidence and supporting artifacts assigned by the Applicant or Organization Administrator.

The Evidence Contributor contributes operational information supporting certification.

The Evidence Contributor does not coordinate workflow ownership.

The Evidence Contributor does not perform governance activities.

The Evidence Contributor does not perform certification activities.

The Evidence Contributor does not perform publication activities.

The Evidence Contributor operates exclusively within constitutionally authorized workflow responsibilities.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# OPERATIONAL PURPOSE

The Evidence Contributor ensures that accurate, complete, traceable, and well-organized evidence is available for operational review.

The Evidence Contributor supports operational readiness through high-quality documentation and repository management.

Evidence Contributors contribute operational inputs rather than constitutional decisions.

---

# PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

The Evidence Contributor shall:

* Prepare assigned evidence.
* Prepare supporting artifacts.
* Verify evidence quality.
* Verify documentation accuracy.
* Maintain repository organization.
* Respond to evidence requests.
* Support remediation activities.
* Coordinate with the Applicant.
* Coordinate with the Organization Administrator.
* Reduce operational review delays.

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Evidence Contributor operations are considered successful when:

* Assigned evidence is complete.
* Supporting artifacts are complete.
* Documentation is accurate.
* Repository organization remains consistent.
* Requested evidence is submitted on time.
* Evidence supports operational review.
* Repository quality remains high.
* Remediation documentation is complete.

---

# ENTRY CONDITIONS

Evidence Contributor operational work begins when:

* Authentication succeeds.
* Organization authorization is verified.
* Evidence Contributor privileges are confirmed.
* Assigned work becomes available.

Operational work begins from the Dashboard.

---

# DAILY OPERATIONAL WORKFLOW

The Evidence Contributor should perform the following operational sequence during every working session.

1. Sign in.
2. Review Dashboard.
3. Review Notifications.
4. Review Assigned Cases.
5. Open assigned Case Workspace.
6. Review Current Workflow Stage.
7. Review assigned evidence tasks.
8. Prepare required documentation.
9. Upload evidence and artifacts.
10. Verify repository completeness.
11. Review outstanding assignments before ending the session.

---

# CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Evidence Contributor is currently responsible for:

* Evidence preparation.
* Artifact preparation.
* Documentation quality.
* Repository organization.
* Evidence updates.
* Supporting remediation.
* Supporting Applicant activities.
* Supporting Organization Administrator activities.

Evidence Contributors remain responsible only for assigned operational activities.

---

# SUPPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES

The Evidence Contributor supports:

* Applicant.
* Organization Administrator.
* GAFAIG Operations Reviewer.

Support activities include:

* Evidence preparation.
* Documentation updates.
* Repository organization.
* Corrective documentation.
* Supporting operational clarification.

Supporting responsibilities never transfer workflow ownership.

---

# REPOSITORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Evidence Contributor participates within:

Evidence Repository

* Prepare evidence.
* Upload assigned evidence.
* Organize evidence.
* Replace outdated documentation.

Artifact Repository

* Upload supporting artifacts.
* Maintain artifact organization.

Information Request Repository

* Prepare supporting documentation.

Remediation Repository

* Prepare corrective evidence.
* Support remediation documentation.

Progress Repository

* Monitor assigned operational activities.

Evidence Contributors support repository readiness but do not review repository submissions.

---

# DECISION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Evidence Contributor does not create constitutional decisions.

The Evidence Contributor supports operational decision making by providing:

* Accurate evidence.
* Supporting artifacts.
* Corrective documentation.
* Clarifying information.

Decision authority remains with authorized GAFAIG participants.

---

# COMMUNICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

Evidence Contributors communicate through authorized operational channels.

Communication responsibilities include:

* Coordinating evidence preparation.
* Responding to assigned requests.
* Clarifying submitted documentation.
* Supporting remediation preparation.
* Coordinating with organizational participants.

Communication shall remain timely, accurate, and traceable.

---

# NOTIFICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

Evidence Contributors shall review notifications at the beginning of every operational session.

Notifications may include:

* Evidence assignments.
* Artifact requests.
* Information requests.
* Deficiency support requests.
* Repository updates.
* Workflow changes.
* Organizational reminders.

Notifications should be reviewed before beginning repository work.

---

# WAITING CONDITIONS

Evidence Contributors may encounter waiting conditions including:

* Applicant preparation.
* Repository review.
* Operational review.
* Information request evaluation.
* Remediation review.
* Organizational coordination.

During waiting conditions the Evidence Contributor should:

* Organize documentation.
* Verify evidence quality.
* Prepare anticipated supporting materials.
* Review repository organization.
* Coordinate with organizational participants.

---

# ESCALATION PROCEDURES

Evidence Contributors should escalate operational issues when:

* Required evidence cannot be obtained.
* Repository uploads repeatedly fail.
* Assigned documentation is unavailable.
* Organizational coordination prevents completion.
* Repository inconsistencies are identified.
* Operational workflow appears blocked.

Escalation shall follow established GAFAIG operational procedures.

---

# OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Evidence Contributors are expected to:

* Maintain evidence quality.
* Preserve repository organization.
* Respond promptly to assignments.
* Prepare accurate documentation.
* Minimize operational delays.
* Support efficient operational review.
* Maintain documentation traceability.

High-quality evidence directly improves operational review efficiency.

---

# OPERATIONAL FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

Evidence Contributors shall always remember:

* Evidence supports workflow.
* Repositories support workflow.
* Documentation quality determines review efficiency.
* The Case Workspace remains the operational center.
* Decisions belong to authorized reviewers.
* Responsibility transfers only through deterministic workflow progression.
* Repository organization improves operational quality.

---

# AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES

Evidence Contributors shall never:

* Perform governance review.
* Record governance findings.
* Accept or reject evidence.
* Issue deficiencies.
* Approve remediation.
* Issue certifications.
* Publish registry records.
* Modify constitutional records.
* Override Snowflake-backed operational data.

Evidence Contributors participate exclusively within constitutionally authorized operational responsibilities.

# PASS 2D.1 — GAFAIG INTAKE REVIEWER OPERATIONAL FOUNDATION

---

# GAFAIG INTAKE REVIEWER OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK

This playbook defines the canonical operational procedures for GAFAIG Intake Reviewers participating in the GAFAIG operational workflow.

The GAFAIG Intake Reviewer performs the initial operational validation of submitted certification cases before they enter Operational Review.

The Intake Reviewer verifies submission readiness, repository completeness, workflow eligibility, and intake requirements.

The Intake Reviewer performs operational validation only.

The Intake Reviewer does not perform governance review.

The Intake Reviewer does not perform certification activities.

The Intake Reviewer does not perform publication activities.

The Intake Reviewer operates exclusively within constitutionally authorized workflow responsibilities.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# OPERATIONAL PURPOSE

The GAFAIG Intake Reviewer verifies that submitted certification cases satisfy all operational intake requirements before operational review begins.

The Intake Reviewer protects downstream workflow quality by ensuring that incomplete, invalid, or improperly prepared submissions do not advance prematurely.

Operational validation precedes operational review.

---

# PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

The GAFAIG Intake Reviewer shall:

* Review newly submitted certification cases.
* Validate submission completeness.
* Verify required repositories exist.
* Verify required organizational information.
* Verify workflow readiness.
* Identify missing intake requirements.
* Route complete cases to Operational Review.
* Return incomplete cases through authorized workflow.
* Maintain operational intake quality.
* Support efficient workflow progression.

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Intake Review operations are considered successful when:

* Submitted cases satisfy intake requirements.
* Repository completeness is verified.
* Required documentation is present.
* Workflow readiness is confirmed.
* Incomplete submissions are identified early.
* Cases advance only when operationally ready.
* Operational Review receives complete certification cases.
* Intake processing remains consistent and deterministic.

---

# ENTRY CONDITIONS

Intake Reviewer operational work begins when:

* Reviewer authentication succeeds.
* GAFAIG operational authorization is verified.
* Intake Reviewer privileges are confirmed.
* Assigned intake queue becomes available.

Every operational session begins from the Intake Dashboard.

---

# DAILY OPERATIONAL WORKFLOW

The Intake Reviewer should perform the following operational sequence during every working session.

1. Sign in.
2. Review Intake Dashboard.
3. Review Intake Queue.
4. Prioritize newly submitted cases.
5. Open assigned Case Workspace.
6. Review Current Workflow Stage.
7. Validate repository completeness.
8. Verify intake readiness.
9. Determine appropriate workflow outcome.
10. Record operational actions.
11. Continue with the next assigned case.

---

# CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer is currently responsible for:

* Intake validation.
* Submission completeness review.
* Repository readiness review.
* Initial workflow validation.
* Intake communication.
* Workflow routing.
* Operational quality control.
* Case acceptance readiness.

The Intake Reviewer remains responsible until deterministic workflow progression transfers responsibility.

---

# SUPPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer supports:

* Applicants.
* Organization Administrators.
* Evidence Contributors.
* GAFAIG Operations Reviewers.

Support activities include:

* Clarifying intake requirements.
* Identifying missing submissions.
* Communicating intake deficiencies.
* Supporting workflow readiness.
* Maintaining operational consistency.

Supporting responsibilities never transfer workflow ownership.

---

# REPOSITORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer validates organizational participation within:

Evidence Repository

* Verify required evidence exists.
* Verify repository completeness.
* Verify organizational readiness.

Artifact Repository

* Verify required supporting artifacts.
* Verify repository organization.

Information Request Repository

* Verify outstanding requests affecting intake.

Remediation Repository

* Verify remediation requirements when applicable.

Progress Repository

* Confirm workflow state supports intake processing.

The Intake Reviewer validates repository readiness but does not perform detailed evidence evaluation.

---

# DECISION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer performs operational intake decisions only.

Operational intake decisions include:

* Intake accepted.
* Intake requires additional information.
* Intake requires correction.
* Intake returned through authorized workflow.
* Intake routed to Operational Review.

The Intake Reviewer does not create governance decisions.

The Intake Reviewer does not determine certification outcomes.

---

# COMMUNICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer communicates through authorized operational channels.

Communication responsibilities include:

* Intake clarification.
* Submission status.
* Missing documentation.
* Workflow routing notifications.
* Operational readiness communication.

Communication shall remain timely, professional, consistent, and fully auditable.

---

# NOTIFICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Intake Reviewer shall review notifications continuously throughout operational sessions.

Notifications may include:

* New case submissions.
* Updated submissions.
* Repository updates.
* Applicant responses.
* Workflow transitions.
* Queue assignments.
* Operational alerts.

Notifications shall be reviewed before processing newly assigned cases.

---

# WAITING CONDITIONS

The Intake Reviewer may encounter waiting conditions including:

* Applicant updates.
* Repository completion.
* Information request responses.
* Organizational corrections.
* Workflow routing.
* Operational queue dependencies.

During waiting conditions the Intake Reviewer should:

* Continue processing other available cases.
* Monitor updated submissions.
* Review queue priorities.
* Prepare pending intake reviews.
* Maintain operational throughput.

---

# ESCALATION PROCEDURES

The Intake Reviewer should escalate operational issues when:

* Required repository information cannot be validated.
* Workflow state is inconsistent.
* Organizational authorization conflicts exist.
* Operational routing cannot proceed.
* System functionality prevents intake review.
* Repeated intake failures indicate systemic issues.

Escalation shall follow established GAFAIG operational procedures.

---

# OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

The Intake Reviewer is expected to:

* Process intake consistently.
* Maintain queue discipline.
* Verify operational readiness.
* Prevent incomplete workflow progression.
* Maintain complete audit history.
* Support efficient operational throughput.
* Preserve deterministic intake decisions.

Effective intake review establishes the operational quality of the entire certification lifecycle.

---

# OPERATIONAL FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

The Intake Reviewer shall always remember:

* Intake protects workflow quality.
* Workflow determines operational progression.
* Repository readiness precedes Operational Review.
* The Case Workspace remains the operational center.
* Operational decisions support constitutional authority.
* Responsibility transfers only through deterministic workflow progression.
* Consistent intake review improves downstream operational efficiency.

---

# AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES

The Intake Reviewer shall never:

* Perform governance review.
* Record governance findings.
* Evaluate evidence beyond intake readiness.
* Issue certifications.
* Publish registry records.
* Modify constitutional records.
* Override Snowflake-backed operational data.
* Circumvent workflow progression.

The Intake Reviewer participates exclusively within constitutionally authorized operational responsibilities.

---

# TRANSITION TO SCREEN-BY-SCREEN GUIDANCE

The following section defines deterministic operational guidance for every Intake Reviewer workspace.

Each operational screen specifies:

* Purpose.
* Entry conditions.
* Review priorities.
* Required operational activities.
* Success indicators.
* Warning indicators.
* Exit conditions.
* Next navigation.

These procedures establish standardized operational behavior throughout the complete GAFAIG Intake Reviewer operational experience.

END PASS 2D.1

# PASS 2D.2 — GAFAIG INTAKE REVIEWER SCREEN-BY-SCREEN OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE

---

# INTAKE REVIEWER DASHBOARD

## Purpose

The Intake Reviewer Dashboard provides operational awareness for all assigned intake activities.

It is the required starting point for every Intake Reviewer work session.

---

## When to Open

Open the Dashboard:

* Immediately after signing in.
* At the beginning of every operational session.
* After receiving new assignments.
* After completing an intake review.
* Before reviewing queue priorities.

---

## Review First

Always review in this order:

1. New Case Submissions.
2. Intake Queue Summary.
3. Priority Cases.
4. SLA Warnings.
5. Blocked Cases.
6. Notifications.
7. Operational Metrics.

---

## Success Indicators

The Dashboard indicates healthy intake operations when:

* New submissions are visible.
* Queue priorities are current.
* No unexplained blocked cases exist.
* SLA targets remain within acceptable limits.
* Intake workload is balanced.

---

## Warning Indicators

Review immediately when:

* Intake queue grows unexpectedly.
* SLA warnings appear.
* Cases remain unassigned.
* Workflow routing fails.
* Multiple blocked cases accumulate.
* Repository validation errors increase.

---

## Required Actions

The Intake Reviewer should:

* Review operational priorities.
* Select the highest-priority intake case.
* Open the Intake Queue.
* Begin intake validation.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Processing low-priority cases before urgent cases.
* Ignoring SLA warnings.
* Leaving newly submitted cases unreviewed.
* Bypassing queue prioritization.

---

## Next Navigation

Dashboard

↓

Intake Queue

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Dashboard review is complete when:

* Queue priorities reviewed.
* Highest-priority case selected.
* Case Workspace opened.

---

# INTAKE QUEUE

## Purpose

The Intake Queue organizes certification cases awaiting intake validation.

---

## When to Open

Open when:

* Beginning operational review.
* Selecting the next assignment.
* Monitoring queue workload.
* Reviewing intake priorities.

---

## Review First

Review:

* Submission time.
* Priority level.
* Workflow stage.
* Organization.
* Current status.
* Waiting duration.

---

## Success Indicators

Queue displays:

* Correct prioritization.
* Current workflow states.
* Clear assignments.
* Expected workload.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Cases remain in queue too long.
* Priorities appear incorrect.
* Workflow states conflict.
* Assignment ownership unclear.

---

## Required Actions

Select the highest-priority eligible case.

Open the Case Workspace.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Selecting cases out of operational priority.
* Ignoring waiting time.
* Processing duplicate submissions.

---

## Next Navigation

Intake Queue

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Case selected for intake validation.

---

# CASE WORKSPACE

## Purpose

The Case Workspace is the primary intake review workspace.

All intake validation activities begin here.

---

## When to Open

Always before reviewing repositories.

---

## Review First

Review in this order:

1. Current Workflow Stage.
2. Applicant Information.
3. Organization Information.
4. Repository Summary.
5. Timeline.
6. Current Responsible Participant.
7. Next Required Action.

---

## Success Indicators

Case Workspace displays:

* Complete submission.
* Expected workflow stage.
* Repository summaries.
* Current ownership.
* No unexplained blocking conditions.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Required repositories missing.
* Workflow stage inconsistent.
* Organizational information incomplete.
* Timeline conflicts exist.
* Submission appears incomplete.

---

## Required Actions

Perform intake validation only.

Determine whether the case is operationally ready to advance.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Performing detailed evidence review.
* Performing governance review.
* Skipping repository validation.
* Advancing incomplete submissions.

---

## Next Navigation

Required Repository Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Initial intake validation complete.

## Purpose

---

## Review First

* Repository completeness.
* Required evidence categories.
* Missing evidence.
* Repository organization.

---

## Success Indicators

Repository contains:

* Required evidence.
* Expected organization.
* No obvious omissions.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Required evidence missing.
* Repository incomplete.
* Duplicate evidence apparent.
* Repository organization inconsistent.

---

Validate operational completeness only.

Do not evaluate evidence quality beyond intake readiness.

---

# ARTIFACT REPOSITORY

* Required artifacts.

## Exit Criteria

## Purpose

## Review First

## Exit Criteria

Remediation status confirmed.

# PROGRESS REPOSITORY

## Purpose

## Review First

* Current workflow stage.
* Completed stages.

* Responsibility transfers.

---

## Required Actions

Verify workflow state supports intake progression.

---

## Exit Criteria

Workflow progression confirmed.

# INTAKE ROUTING

## Purpose

* Repository readiness.

# GAFAIG OPERATIONS REVIEWER OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK

This playbook defines the canonical operational procedures for GAFAIG Operations Reviewers participating in the GAFAIG Operational Workflow.

The GAFAIG Operations Reviewer performs the complete operational review of certification cases following successful intake validation.

The Operations Reviewer verifies operational completeness, coordinates applicant interactions, evaluates repository readiness, manages operational deficiencies, reviews remediation submissions, and determines operational readiness for Governance Review.

The Operations Reviewer performs operational review only.

The Operations Reviewer does not perform governance review.

The Operations Reviewer does not issue certification.

The Operations Reviewer does not authorize publication.

The Operations Reviewer operates exclusively within constitutionally authorized workflow responsibilities.

Snowflake remains the source of truth.

Human governance authority remains supreme.

---

# OPERATIONAL PURPOSE

The GAFAIG Operations Reviewer performs the comprehensive operational evaluation required to determine whether a certification case is operationally complete and ready for Governance Review.

Operational Review verifies that the applicant has satisfied all operational requirements before constitutional governance activities begin.

Operational Review protects governance by ensuring reviewers receive complete, organized, and operationally validated certification cases.

---

# PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

The GAFAIG Operations Reviewer shall:

* Review operational completeness.
* Review repository readiness.
* Evaluate evidence sufficiency for operational purposes.
* Verify supporting artifacts.
* Identify missing operational information.
* Issue Information Requests when clarification is required.
* Issue Deficiencies when operational requirements are not satisfied.
* Review remediation submissions.
* Verify remediation completeness.
* Determine operational readiness.
* Route qualified cases to Governance Review.
* Maintain complete operational documentation.

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Operations Review is considered successful when:

* Operational requirements have been satisfied.
* Repository readiness has been verified.
* Required documentation is complete.
* Operational issues have been resolved.
* Information Requests have been satisfied.
* Deficiencies have been resolved.
* Remediation has been accepted when required.
* Governance Review receives a complete operationally validated case.
* Workflow progresses without avoidable operational interruptions.

---

# ENTRY CONDITIONS

Operations Reviewer operational work begins when:

* Reviewer authentication succeeds.
* GAFAIG operational authorization is verified.
* Operations Reviewer privileges are confirmed.
* Assigned Operational Review Queue becomes available.
* Intake Review has successfully completed.

Every operational session begins from the Operations Dashboard.

---

# DAILY OPERATIONAL WORKFLOW

The Operations Reviewer should perform the following operational sequence during every working session.

1. Sign in.
2. Review Operations Dashboard.
3. Review Operational Review Queue.
4. Prioritize assigned certification cases.
5. Open assigned Case Workspace.
6. Review Current Workflow Stage.
7. Review repository summaries.
8. Evaluate operational readiness.
9. Perform required operational actions.
10. Document operational findings.
11. Continue with the next assigned case.

---

# CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Operations Reviewer is currently responsible for:

* Operational Review.
* Repository evaluation.
* Operational completeness validation.
* Information Request management.
* Deficiency management.
* Remediation review.
* Operational communication.
* Workflow progression.
* Operational readiness determination.
* Governance handoff preparation.

Responsibility remains with the Operations Reviewer until deterministic workflow progression transfers ownership.

---

# SUPPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES

The Operations Reviewer supports:

* Applicants.
* Organization Administrators.
* Evidence Contributors.
* Governance Reviewers.

Support activities include:

* Clarifying operational expectations.
* Coordinating repository completion.
* Reviewing applicant responses.
* Guiding operational remediation.
* Preparing governance-ready cases.

Supporting responsibilities never transfer constitutional authority.

---

# REPOSITORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Operations Reviewer performs operational review of:

Evidence Repository

* Review operational completeness.
* Verify required evidence categories.
* Identify missing operational evidence.

Artifact Repository

* Review supporting artifacts.
* Verify artifact readiness.

Information Request Repository

* Create Information Requests.
* Review responses.
* Close completed requests.

Deficiency Repository

* Issue deficiencies.
* Track corrective actions.
* Verify deficiency resolution.

Remediation Repository

* Review remediation submissions.
* Verify corrective documentation.
* Determine operational readiness.

Certification Repository

* Monitor operational certification progression.

Progress Repository

* Monitor workflow progression.
* Verify operational state.

Repository review supports operational evaluation and does not replace constitutional governance.

---

# DECISION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Operations Reviewer performs operational decisions including:

* Operational Review complete.
* Additional information required.
* Deficiency required.
* Remediation required.
* Operational readiness achieved.
* Ready for Governance Review.

The Operations Reviewer shall never:

* Record governance findings.
* Determine governance outcomes.
* Issue certifications.
* Publish registry records.

Constitutional authority remains separate from operational authority.

---

# COMMUNICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Operations Reviewer communicates exclusively through authorized operational channels.

Communication responsibilities include:

* Information Requests.
* Deficiency Notices.
* Remediation guidance.
* Workflow updates.
* Operational clarification.
* Readiness notifications.

Operational communication shall remain professional, consistent, deterministic, and fully auditable.

---

# NOTIFICATION RESPONSIBILITIES

Operations Reviewers shall monitor notifications continuously throughout operational sessions.

Notifications may include:

* New Operational Review assignments.
* Applicant responses.
* Repository updates.
* Information Request responses.
* Deficiency responses.
* Remediation submissions.
* Queue assignments.
* Operational alerts.

Notifications shall be reviewed before processing each assigned case.

---

# WAITING CONDITIONS

The Operations Reviewer may encounter waiting conditions including:

* Applicant response preparation.
* Information Request responses.
* Repository updates.
* Deficiency correction.
* Remediation preparation.
* Governance queue availability.
* Operational dependencies.

During waiting conditions the Operations Reviewer should:

* Continue processing other assigned cases.
* Monitor pending responses.
* Review queue priorities.
* Prepare governance-ready cases.
* Maintain operational throughput.

---

# ESCALATION PROCEDURES

The Operations Reviewer should escalate operational issues when:

* Operational workflow cannot proceed.
* Repository integrity cannot be verified.
* Repeated applicant failures occur.
* System functionality prevents operational review.
* Workflow state becomes inconsistent.
* Operational dependencies prevent progression.
* Governance handoff cannot be completed.

Escalation shall follow established GAFAIG operational procedures.

---

# OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

The Operations Reviewer is expected to:

* Maintain consistent operational review quality.
* Preserve deterministic workflow progression.
* Maintain complete operational documentation.
* Process certification cases efficiently.
* Minimize avoidable workflow delays.
* Maintain repository review quality.
* Prepare governance-ready certification cases.
* Preserve complete audit history.

Effective Operational Review establishes the quality of Governance Review.

---

# OPERATIONAL FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

The Operations Reviewer shall always remember:

* Operational Review validates readiness rather than governance.
* Repository completeness precedes Governance Review.
* Information Requests clarify.
* Deficiencies require corrective action.
* Remediation restores operational readiness.
* Workflow determines operational progression.
* The Case Workspace remains the operational center.
* Responsibility transfers only through deterministic workflow progression.
* Constitutional authority remains separate from operational authority.

---

# AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES

The Operations Reviewer shall never:

* Perform governance review.
* Record governance findings.
* Determine governance outcomes.
* Issue certifications.
* Publish registry records.
* Modify constitutional records.
* Override Snowflake-backed operational data.
* Circumvent workflow progression.

The Operations Reviewer participates exclusively within constitutionally authorized operational responsibilities.

---

# TRANSITION TO SCREEN-BY-SCREEN GUIDANCE

The following section defines deterministic operational guidance for every Operations Reviewer workspace.

Each operational screen specifies:

* Purpose.
* Entry conditions.
* Review priorities.
* Required operational activities.
* Success indicators.
* Warning indicators.
* Exit conditions.
* Next navigation.

These procedures establish standardized operational behavior throughout the complete GAFAIG Operations Reviewer operational experience.

END PASS 2E.1

# PASS 2E.2 — GAFAIG OPERATIONS REVIEWER SCREEN-BY-SCREEN OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE

---

# OPERATIONS REVIEWER DASHBOARD

## Purpose

The Operations Reviewer Dashboard provides operational awareness for all assigned certification reviews.

It is the required starting point for every Operations Reviewer work session.

---

## When to Open

Open the Dashboard:

* Immediately after signing in.
* At the beginning of every operational session.
* After receiving notifications.
* After completing an operational review.
* Before selecting the next assigned case.

---

## Review First

Always review in this order:

1. Assigned Review Queue.
2. Priority Cases.
3. SLA Warnings.
4. Waiting Cases.
5. Information Request Responses.
6. Remediation Submissions.
7. Operational Notifications.
8. Performance Metrics.

---

## Success Indicators

The Dashboard indicates healthy operations when:

* Assigned queue is current.
* High-priority cases are clearly identified.
* No unexplained blocked cases exist.
* SLA targets remain within acceptable limits.
* Workflow progression is current.

---

## Warning Indicators

Review immediately when:

* SLA deadlines approach.
* Multiple cases remain blocked.
* Information Requests remain unanswered.
* Remediation reviews are overdue.
* Queue backlog increases.
* Workflow progression stalls.

---

## Required Actions

The Operations Reviewer should:

* Review operational priorities.
* Select the highest-priority case.
* Open the Operational Review Queue.
* Begin operational review.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Reviewing cases out of priority order.
* Ignoring overdue cases.
* Delaying applicant responses.
* Leaving completed cases in the active queue.

---

## Next Navigation

Dashboard

↓

Operational Review Queue

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Dashboard review is complete when:

* Priorities reviewed.
* Case selected.
* Case Workspace opened.

---

# OPERATIONAL REVIEW QUEUE

## Purpose

The Operational Review Queue organizes certification cases awaiting operational review.

---

## When to Open

Open when:

* Beginning operational review.
* Selecting the next assignment.
* Reviewing workload.
* Monitoring queue priorities.

---

## Review First

Review:

* Priority.
* Workflow stage.
* Submission age.
* Current status.
* Waiting duration.
* Current owner.

---

## Success Indicators

Queue displays:

* Accurate priorities.
* Expected workflow stages.
* Current assignments.
* Balanced workload.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Cases remain inactive.
* Priorities appear inconsistent.
* Workflow state conflicts exist.
* Ownership appears incorrect.

---

## Required Actions

Select the highest-priority operational review.

---

## Next Navigation

Operational Review Queue

↓

Case Workspace

---

## Exit Criteria

Operational review begins.

---

# CASE WORKSPACE

## Purpose

The Case Workspace is the primary operational review environment.

All operational decisions originate here.

---

## When to Open

Always before reviewing repositories.

---

## Review First

Review in this order:

1. Current Workflow Stage.
2. Operational Timeline.
3. Current Responsible Participant.
4. Repository Summary.
5. Outstanding Information Requests.
6. Outstanding Deficiencies.
7. Remediation Status.
8. Next Required Action.

---

## Success Indicators

Case Workspace displays:

* Complete operational context.
* Current workflow state.
* Repository summaries.
* Operational history.
* Expected ownership.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Repository summaries incomplete.
* Timeline inconsistent.
* Workflow blocked.
* Operational history incomplete.
* Required actions unclear.

---

## Required Actions

Perform only operational review activities authorized for the current workflow stage.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Beginning governance review.
* Ignoring previous operational history.
* Skipping repository summaries.
* Bypassing workflow requirements.

---

## Next Navigation

Required Repository Workspace.

---

## Exit Criteria

Current operational activity completed.

---

# EVIDENCE REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Evaluate operational evidence readiness.

---

## When to Open

Whenever evidence evaluation is required.

---

## Review First

Review:

* Required evidence.
* Repository completeness.
* Evidence organization.
* Supporting documentation.
* Outstanding evidence issues.

---

## Success Indicators

Repository contains:

* Complete evidence.
* Expected organization.
* Required documentation.
* Traceable submissions.

---

## Warning Indicators

Investigate when:

* Required evidence missing.
* Duplicate evidence exists.
* Repository disorganized.
* Documentation inconsistent.

---

## Required Actions

Evaluate operational sufficiency.

Determine whether additional evidence is required.

---

## Common Operational Mistakes

Avoid:

* Performing governance evaluation.
* Ignoring repository organization.
* Overlooking supporting documentation.

---

## Next Navigation

Return to Case Workspace.

---

## Exit Criteria

Operational evidence evaluation completed.

---

# ARTIFACT REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Review supporting operational artifacts.

## Review First

* Required artifacts.
* Supporting documentation.
* Repository completeness.

## Required Actions

Determine whether artifacts adequately support operational review.

## Exit Criteria

Artifact review completed.

---

# INFORMATION REQUEST WORKSPACE

## Purpose

Manage operational clarification requests.

---

## Review First

* Outstanding requests.
* Applicant responses.
* Supporting documentation.
* Response completeness.

---

## Required Actions

Determine whether clarification requirements have been satisfied.

Issue additional requests only when operationally justified.

---

## Exit Criteria

Information Request resolved or updated.

---

# DEFICIENCY WORKSPACE

## Purpose

Manage operational deficiencies.

---

## Review First

* Outstanding deficiencies.
* Required corrective actions.
* Supporting documentation.
* Workflow impact.

---

## Required Actions

Determine whether deficiencies remain valid.

Verify corrective actions.

---

## Exit Criteria

Deficiency resolved or remains active.

---

# REMEDIATION WORKSPACE

## Purpose

Review remediation submissions.

---

## Review First

* Submitted remediation.
* Corrective documentation.
* Repository updates.
* Outstanding operational concerns.

---

## Required Actions

Determine whether remediation satisfies operational requirements.

---

## Exit Criteria

Remediation accepted or additional action required.

---

# CERTIFICATION READINESS

## Purpose

Determine whether the certification case is operationally ready for Governance Review.

---

## Review First

* Repository completeness.
* Outstanding issues.
* Operational history.
* Remaining workflow requirements.

---

## Required Actions

Determine one of the following:

* Ready for Governance Review.
* Additional operational work required.
* Information Request required.
* Deficiency required.
* Remediation required.

---

## Exit Criteria

Operational readiness determination completed.

---

# PROGRESS REPOSITORY

## Purpose

Monitor workflow progression.

---

## Review First

* Current workflow stage.
* Completed stages.
* Waiting stages.
* Timeline.
* Responsibility transfers.

---

## Required Actions

Verify workflow progression remains deterministic.

---

## Exit Criteria

Workflow state confirmed.

---

# GOVERNANCE HANDOFF

## Purpose

Transfer operationally complete certification cases to Governance Review.

---

## Review First

* Operational readiness.
* Repository completeness.
* Outstanding operational actions.
* Workflow eligibility.

---

## Required Actions

Verify:

* Operational Review complete.
* Required repositories complete.
* Outstanding operational work resolved.
* Governance handoff authorized.

Record operational completion.

---

## Exit Criteria

Responsibility transferred through deterministic workflow progression.

# GAFAIG OPERATIONS REVIEWER OPERATIONAL CHECKLIST

The following checklist shall be completed during every operational review session.

### Session Startup

□ Authenticate successfully.

□ Open Operations Reviewer Dashboard.

□ Review unread notifications.

□ Review Operational Review Queue.

□ Review queue priorities.

□ Review SLA warnings.

□ Review Waiting Conditions.

---

### Queue Management

Before selecting a case:

□ Review operational priority.

□ Review workflow stage.

□ Review submission age.

□ Review current owner.

□ Review outstanding operational dependencies.

Select the highest-priority eligible case.

---

### Initial Operational Review

Before reviewing repositories:

□ Open the Case Workspace.

□ Verify organization identity.

□ Verify applicant information.

□ Verify intake completed successfully.

□ Review operational history.

□ Review workflow timeline.

□ Verify Current Responsible Participant.

---

### Repository Review

Review every repository required for the current workflow stage.

Evidence Repository

□ Repository complete.

□ Required evidence categories present.

□ Repository organized.

Artifact Repository

□ Required artifacts present.

□ Supporting documentation available.

Information Request Repository

□ Outstanding requests reviewed.

□ Responses evaluated.

Deficiency Repository

□ Existing deficiencies reviewed.

□ Outstanding corrective actions identified.

Remediation Repository

□ Remediation submissions reviewed.

□ Corrective documentation evaluated.

Certification Repository

□ Certification progression verified.

Progress Repository

□ Workflow progression confirmed.

---

### Operational Assessment

Before making an operational determination:

□ Repository completeness verified.

□ Operational requirements evaluated.

□ Outstanding operational issues identified.

□ Applicant responses reviewed.

□ Deficiencies evaluated.

□ Remediation reviewed.

□ Workflow state confirmed.

---

### Operational Decision

Determine one authorized operational outcome:

□ Continue Operational Review.

□ Issue Information Request.

□ Issue Deficiency.

□ Accept Remediation.

□ Request additional remediation.

□ Ready for Governance Review.

Document the operational determination.

---

### Governance Preparation

Before transferring responsibility:

□ Operational review complete.

□ Repository readiness verified.

□ Outstanding issues resolved.

□ Workflow progression updated.

□ Operational documentation complete.

---

### Session Completion

Before closing the case:

□ Operational notes complete.

□ Timeline updated.

□ Responsibility transfer confirmed.

□ Queue status updated.

Proceed to the next assigned case.

---
